nodes.definition: Count of occurrences of a term in a document used as the base lexical signal.

pros.claim: raw count is cheap and interpretable

cons.claim: unbounded growth over-rewards repetition
cons.example: a spam doc repeating a word 1000x dominates

nodes.definition: Sublinear term-frequency transform 1+log(tf) that damps the contribution of repeated terms.

pros.claim: damps runaway repetition with one cheap transform

cons.claim: fixed curve cannot adapt to document length
cons.example: long docs still over-weighted vs short

nodes.definition: Augmented tf (a+(1-a)*tf/maxtf) and boolean tf (0/1) variants that bound or binarize the term signal.

pros.claim: augmented tf controls per-doc dominance via max-tf anchor
pros.example: a=0.5 floor on all present terms

cons.claim: max-tf normalization is sensitive to a single outlier term

nodes.definition: Global term-discrimination weight log(N/df) that down-weights terms appearing in many documents.

pros.claim: captures term specificity with one collection statistic

cons.claim: ignores within-document salience entirely
cons.example: df-only weight blind to local frequency

nodes.definition: RSJ-style probabilistic idf log((N-df+0.5)/(df+0.5)) derived from relevance odds, used as the BM25 idf term.

pros.claim: grounded in relevance-odds derivation

cons.claim: can go negative for very frequent terms
cons.example: df>N/2 yields negative weight needing a floor

nodes.definition: Composite weight multiplying a tf variant by idf to balance local salience against global specificity.

pros.claim: simple multiplicative balance of two orthogonal signals

cons.claim: lacks principled length normalization and saturation
cons.example: loses to BM25 on TREC benchmarks

nodes.definition: Geometric model representing documents and queries as weight vectors scored by cosine similarity.

pros.claim: cosine cancels document length via L2 norm

cons.claim: L2 cosine normalization is a crude length model

nodes.definition: Correction that pivots cosine length normalization around average length to remove systematic short-doc bias.

pros.claim: aligns retrieval probability with relevance probability by length

cons.claim: slope must be tuned per collection

nodes.definition: Okapi BM25 ranking with k1 term-frequency saturation and b document-length normalization over probabilistic idf.

pros.claim: saturating tf with length norm is the strong lexical baseline

cons.claim: two parameters need per-collection tuning
cons.example: b too high crushes long relevant docs

nodes.definition: BM25 query-term-frequency saturation component k3 that damps repeated terms within long queries.

pros.claim: controls verbose-query term inflation
pros.example: k3 caps a thrice-repeated query term

cons.claim: irrelevant for short keyword queries
cons.example: adds a parameter rarely worth tuning

nodes.definition: BM25+ adds a delta lower-bound so long documents containing a query term never score below short documents lacking it.

pros.claim: fixes BM25 over-penalization of long documents

cons.claim: adds delta parameter with modest gains

nodes.definition: Fielded BM25 that combines per-field term frequencies with field weights and per-field length normalization before saturation.

pros.claim: models title vs body importance correctly

cons.claim: field weights and per-field b multiply tuning burden

nodes.definition: DFR framework scoring terms by the information gained over a random distribution, with normalization and first-normalization components.

pros.claim: derives weighting from first information-theoretic principles

cons.claim: multiple interchangeable components confuse tuning

nodes.definition: Language-model retrieval scoring documents by the probability their unigram model generates the query.

pros.claim: principled generative probabilistic foundation

cons.claim: zero probability for unseen query terms without smoothing
cons.example: any missing term zeroes the product

nodes.definition: Bayesian smoothing of the document language model toward the collection model with concentration mu, scaling with document length.

pros.claim: length-adaptive smoothing favors short verbose-free queries

cons.claim: single mu suboptimal across query lengths
cons.example: long queries want more collection mixing

nodes.definition: Linear interpolation smoothing mixing document and collection models by a fixed lambda independent of length.

pros.claim: strong for long verbose queries via constant mixing

cons.claim: length-independent mixing weak for short queries

nodes.definition: Smoothing that first applies Dirichlet for estimation then Jelinek-Mercer for query noise, decoupling the two roles of smoothing.

pros.claim: separates estimation smoothing from query-noise smoothing

cons.claim: two coupled parameters increase tuning cost

nodes.definition: Smoothing that subtracts a fixed discount from each seen term count and redistributes mass to the collection model.

pros.claim: simple constant discount with clear back-off semantics

cons.claim: constant discount less length-adaptive than Dirichlet

nodes.definition: Formal retrieval constraints (TFC term-frequency, LNC length-normalization, TDC term-discrimination) that any sound weighting must satisfy.

pros.claim: predicts model failures analytically before benchmarking

cons.claim: constraint satisfaction does not guarantee top accuracy

nodes.definition: Design principle that term-frequency contribution must asymptotically saturate so additional occurrences yield diminishing score gains.

pros.claim: prevents single-term repetition from dominating relevance

cons.claim: over-saturation discards genuine frequency signal
cons.example: k1 near zero collapses to boolean

nodes.definition: The tradeoff between penalizing verbose documents and preserving recall on long relevant documents across normalization schemes.

pros.claim: makes the recall vs precision length tradeoff explicit
pros.example: guides b vs delta vs slope choice

cons.claim: optimal point is collection and task dependent

edges.why_related: log tf is a transform applied on top of raw counts
edges.resolution_rule: recompute log tf when counts rebuild

edges.why_related: augmented and boolean tf derive from raw counts
edges.benefit_of_coupling: single count pass feeds all tf variants
edges.resolution_rule: tie all tf variants to one count source

edges.why_related: both are core term statistics but neither requires the other
edges.benefit_of_coupling: planning the weighting needs both signals
edges.example: tf is local, idf is global
edges.resolution_rule: keep tf and idf computation independent

edges.why_related: probabilistic idf is a variant of the document-frequency weight
edges.resolution_rule: prefer prob idf inside BM25, classic idf in VSM

edges.why_related: tf-idf multiplies a tf variant by idf
edges.resolution_rule: fix tf variant before computing tf-idf

edges.why_related: tf-idf multiplies tf by the idf weight
edges.resolution_rule: recompute tf-idf when idf changes

edges.why_related: cosine scoring consumes tf-idf weight vectors
edges.resolution_rule: guard against zero-norm vectors

edges.why_related: pivoted normalization corrects cosine length bias
edges.resolution_rule: retune slope when corpus shifts

edges.why_related: BM25 uses probabilistic idf as its term weight
edges.resolution_rule: floor prob idf before BM25 scoring

edges.why_related: BM25 saturates raw term frequency
edges.resolution_rule: rebuild BM25 on count change

edges.why_related: saturation design constrains BM25 k1 behavior
edges.resolution_rule: tune k1 to satisfy saturation constraint

edges.why_related: k3 extends BM25 to query-term saturation
edges.resolution_rule: enable k3 only for verbose queries

edges.why_related: BM25+ adds a lower bound to BM25 scores
edges.resolution_rule: tune delta to fix long-doc penalty only

edges.why_related: BM25F generalizes BM25 to multiple fields
edges.resolution_rule: combine field tf pre-saturation

edges.why_related: BM25 b parameter directly sets the length-normalization tradeoff point
edges.risk_of_conflict: b mis-set causes systematic length bias
edges.resolution_rule: resolve tradeoff before locking b

edges.why_related: pivot slope is one realization of the length tradeoff
edges.benefit_of_coupling: links VSM normalization to the tradeoff
edges.resolution_rule: analyze tradeoff across schemes jointly

edges.why_related: query likelihood requires smoothing; Dirichlet is one method
edges.resolution_rule: pick smoothing before LM scoring

edges.why_related: query likelihood requires smoothing; JM is one method
edges.resolution_rule: pick smoothing before LM scoring

edges.why_related: query likelihood requires smoothing; absolute discounting is one method
edges.risk_of_conflict: negative mass if discount too big
edges.resolution_rule: bound discount below min count

edges.why_related: two-stage smoothing applies Dirichlet first
edges.resolution_rule: set lambda=0 to recover Dirichlet

edges.why_related: two-stage smoothing applies JM second for query noise
edges.example: JM stage on top of Dirichlet
edges.resolution_rule: tune mu then lambda

edges.why_related: Dirichlet and JM are competing single-method smoothers
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing wrong method hurts a query class
edges.resolution_rule: Dirichlet for short queries, JM for long, else two-stage

edges.why_related: Dirichlet and absolute discounting are alternative smoothers
edges.resolution_rule: prefer Dirichlet unless back-off semantics needed

edges.why_related: tf-idf and BM25 are competing lexical scoring models
edges.benefit_of_coupling: forces a model choice for the ranker
edges.resolution_rule: default to BM25; keep tf-idf only as a lightweight fallback

edges.why_related: geometric VSM and probabilistic LM are competing scoring paradigms
edges.resolution_rule: choose paradigm per task; do not blend scores naively

edges.why_related: BM25 and DFR are competing probabilistic weighting models
edges.resolution_rule: default BM25 unless DFR wins local benchmark

edges.why_related: DFR uses collection-level term statistics akin to idf
edges.resolution_rule: recompute DFR stats with collection updates

edges.why_related: DFR scores transform raw term frequency
edges.resolution_rule: rebuild DFR on count change

edges.why_related: TFC constraints formalize the saturation requirement
edges.resolution_rule: validate saturation curve against TFC

edges.why_related: LNC constraints formalize length-normalization requirements
edges.resolution_rule: check schemes against LNC before locking

edges.why_related: TDC constraint formalizes term-discrimination via idf
edges.resolution_rule: ensure idf satisfies TDC

edges.why_related: LNC2 lower-bound constraint motivates the BM25+ delta
edges.resolution_rule: apply delta to meet lower-bound constraint

edges.why_related: log tf is an early instance of saturation thinking
edges.benefit_of_coupling: links variant to the general principle
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating them as identical loses BM25 nuance
edges.resolution_rule: use saturation design to generalize beyond log

edges.why_related: saturation and length normalization both reshape tf and can over-correct jointly
edges.benefit_of_coupling: surfaces interaction between the two knobs
edges.resolution_rule: tune k1 and b jointly, not independently

edges.why_related: Dirichlet-smoothed LM and BM25 are parallel strong baselines
edges.risk_of_conflict: running both without comparison wastes effort
edges.resolution_rule: benchmark both, deploy the winner

edges.why_related: both encode collection-level discrimination differently
edges.resolution_rule: keep probabilistic frameworks distinct

edges.why_related: per-field length normalization in BM25F instantiates the tradeoff per field
edges.resolution_rule: tune per-field b within the tradeoff frame

conflict_axes.trigger: selecting the primary lexical ranking model
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: BM25 dominates by default; tf-idf retained only as a lightweight fallback
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: tf-idf wins local benchmark by a significant ndcg margin
conflict_axes.example: BM25 chosen as default ranker; tf-idf documented as fallback for low-resource indexing

conflict_axes.trigger: choosing a scoring paradigm for the ranker
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: probabilistic models dominate for accuracy; VSM kept for interpretability
conflict_axes.example: select one paradigm per task; do not naively blend cosine and likelihood scores

conflict_axes.trigger: selecting an LM smoothing method for a query workload
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Dirichlet for short queries, JM for long, two-stage for mixed workloads
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: single method underperforms on a dominant query class
conflict_axes.example: route by query-length distribution; default two-stage when mixed

conflict_axes.trigger: setting how strongly term frequency saturates
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: saturation must bound repetition without erasing frequency signal
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: k1 near zero collapses scoring to boolean presence
conflict_axes.example: tune k1 so marginal gain decreases yet stays positive across realistic tf

conflict_axes.dominance_logic: normalization must not over-penalize long relevant documents nor over-retrieve short ones
conflict_axes.example: tune b/slope on relevance judgments; add BM25+ delta if lower-bound violated

conflict_axes.trigger: deciding whether to trust tuned parameters or formal constraints
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: constraints gate which tuned configurations are admissible
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a tuned configuration violates a core IR constraint
conflict_axes.example: reject tuned settings that violate TFC/LNC/TDC even if they win a single metric

conflict_axes.trigger: choosing the idf form for a given model
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: probabilistic idf inside BM25, classic idf inside VSM tf-idf
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: probabilistic idf yields negative weights on frequent terms
conflict_axes.example: use probabilistic idf with a non-negativity floor in BM25; classic idf in cosine VSM

conflict_axes.trigger: deciding whether to adopt fielded weighting
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: adopt BM25F only when field structure materially affects relevance
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: field-weight tuning overfits and degrades held-out ndcg
conflict_axes.example: adopt BM25F only with enough judgments to tune field weights without overfitting

conflict_axes.trigger: deciding whether to model query-term frequency
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: enable k3 only when verbose repeated-term queries occur
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: query logs show frequent multi-occurrence query terms
conflict_axes.example: enable k3 for verbose-query workloads; disable for keyword queries
